content:
Consider the following.

example:
  True →
  (forall (x: Nat), 0 ≤ x → False) →
  False
:= by
  intro T H
  apply H
  . -- 0 ≤ ?x
    revert T
    intro T
    lia
  . -- Nat
    exact default

After the apply H, we have two goals to fulfill: 0 ≤ ?x and Nat. These two are easy to prove. However, if I revert T and intro T again, the second goal just disappears. In this case, Lean complains that No goals to be solved for the second bullet (goal Nat), but without it, Lean complains (kernel) declaration has metavariables '_example'.

I think the reason is that after apply H, the two goals both rely on T. More precisely, the first goal 0 ≤ ?x (some MVarId) depends on the second goal Nat, which is exactly the hole in goal 0 ≤ ?x, and they both have T in their local contexts. So, erasing T in the contexts causes the second goal to crash even though both of them don't really depend on T at all .

The same thing happens if one tries to clear T.

example:
  True →
  (forall (x: Nat), 0 ≤ x → False) →
  False
:= by
  intro T H
  apply H
  . clear T
    lia
  . exact default

This time Lean complains that Tactic clear failed: target depends on 'T'. I think the reason is the same: when we clear T, the clear tactic will find ?x depends on T. (Still, ?x does not really depend on T).

I wonder:

  • How to correct the behavior of revert
  • How to clear the T as no goals rely on it essentially.

I know the best solution is not to write the tactics in such a weird way, but I encountered them when making a tactic on my own. I was following SLF (Separation Logic Foundations, a part of Software Foundations) to make the xsimpl tactic in Lean, which helps to simplify a heap predicate expression (i.e., of type Heap → Prop, where Heap is a partial map Nat → Val from natural numbers to some values).

In this tactic, new hypotheses are introduced and a list of hints dwells in the context and is bing consumed during the simplification. Thus in Rocq, the original xsimpl tactic first poses a dummy ltac_mark and put the list of hints in the local context. After the simplification steps, new hypotheses are introduced (including meta variables) after the mark, so at the end we can revert those introduced by xsimpl and clear the mark. Besides, the hint list is also changed. That means we have to frequently clear the hint list and introduce a modified one.

That is the reason why I encountered with the clear and revert problem: after the simplification, a mark and a hint list was in the context, where there might be several holes relying on them, so I had some trouble removing them.

You can find my code explaining xsimpl here, and more examples here. My current solution is to clear the hint list after each step for those non-simplification goals and repeat any_goals clear_mark at the end of simplification.

They worked fine in most cases, but I still spotted a case where the mark is still there. I also tried to erase the mark without checking the dependencies, but it failed me to check the goal:

Maybe there is another better practice to handle those dummy marks or meta variables that help with the tactics not the proof?
